models_evaluated: deep learning morphological screening aid for FHdRCC

links.outcome: Pathologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance, and overreliance on incorrect AI output
links.effect: AI assistance improved accuracy (60.0–73.3%, P = 0.012) and inter-rater reliability (Fleiss' kappa 0.311–0.482); Receptive group had higher susceptibility to incorrect AI outputs (median CORR 0.800 vs 0.600).
links.quote: AI assistance significantly improved overall diagnostic accuracy (60.0–73.3%, P = 0.012) and inter-rater reliability (Fleiss’ kappa 0.311–0.482).

links.outcome: Clinical overreliance on incorrect AI outputs among pathologists
links.effect: Receptive group (n=14) benefited more from correct AI advice (median RAIR 0.732 vs 0.444) but was more susceptible to incorrect outputs (median CORR 0.800 vs 0.600).
links.quote: The Receptive group derived greater diagnostic benefit from correct AI advice (median RAIR, 0.732 vs. 0.444) but exhibited higher susceptibility to incorrect outputs (median CORR, 0.800 vs. 0.600).

unlisted_practices: Persona-tailored training based on human-AI reliance behavior

screen.reason: Empirical crossover reader study examining pathologists' diagnostic accuracy and behavioral reliance/overreliance patterns with versus without deep learning diagnostic assistance.

primary.practice: AI-assisted reader evaluation (with vs. without AI assistance)
